posts.title: Welcome to your site
posts.excerpt: Explore the sample, then publish your own posts, pages, and menus from ZeroPress Studio.
posts.content:
Your site is ready to receive content from ZeroPress Studio. These sample posts show how writing, images, and navigation look in the blog theme.

## Connect Studio

Follow **Deploy and connect Studio** in your repository's README. Connect Studio to the existing `zeropress-preview-data.json` file, then publish your site.

Publishing replaces the sample posts, pages, menus, and widgets with your Studio content. Your repository keeps the theme and public files.

## Explore the sample

- Open **Categories → Design** in the header to explore the three-level menu.
- Read [Notes on Typography](/posts/notes-on-typography/) for tables, figures, and captions.
- Browse older posts using the page links or the [archive](/archive/).

## Forms and newsletters

The sample includes a [message form](/zp_form/) and a newsletter sign-up in the footer. Both show setup guidance until connected to your ZeroPress Edge service. The README explains which configuration files to edit.

posts.title: Writing in the Margins
posts.excerpt: On keeping a notebook of half-thoughts, and why the best ideas often arrive sideways.
posts.content:
There is a particular kind of quiet that arrives only after the keyboard stops. The cursor blinks, but it is no longer waiting. It is keeping you company.

## On craft

Most of the work that matters happens in the editing. The first draft is just a permission slip — it tells you that the idea exists, that it can survive a sentence.

> Write drunk on the idea. Edit sober on the reader.

## Small habits

I keep a folder of unfinished posts. Some of them are years old. Occasionally one of them turns into something. Usually they just remind me what I was thinking about that month.

### A short list

- Write the title last.
- Read the post out loud before publishing.
- Cut the first paragraph.

## Closing

If you made it this far, thank you. The internet is loud, and your attention is a gift.

posts.title: The Quiet Web
posts.excerpt: A love letter to small, slow, hand-made websites — and the people who still build them.
posts.content:
There is still a quiet web underneath the loud one. Hand-coded pages, weird sidebars, footnotes that lead somewhere personal.

## On craft

The small site is a craft object. It does not have to scale. It just has to be true.

## Small habits

View source. Save the page. Send a kind email to the author. The web rewards small attentions.

posts.title: Notes on Typography
posts.excerpt: What I've learned about line height, measure, and the quiet tyranny of the default font stack.
posts.content:
A comfortable page gives each part of a story enough room. Headings mark a change of thought; a caption keeps an image close to its meaning.

Measure and rhythm

Start with a readable line length, then adjust the spacing. A little emphasis usually does more than another heading. The color reference describes the palette used here.

A small type reference

ElementPurposeStarting point
Body textLong passagesComfortable measure
HeadingsNew sectionsClear hierarchy
CaptionsImage contextShort, useful details

Read it once more

  1. Read a paragraph aloud.
  2. Check the page on a narrow screen.
  3. Remove anything that interrupts the story.

The shape of a page should make reading easier.

Small changes to spacing can matter more than choosing another font.

posts.title: Small Tools, Big Leverage
posts.excerpt: A handful of tiny scripts that quietly run my week. None of them are clever. All of them are mine.
posts.content:
## On craft

The best tool is the one you wrote yesterday for a problem you have today.

```sh
alias todo='vim ~/notes/today.md'
```

## Closing

Keep them small. Replace them often.

posts.title: The Walk
posts.excerpt: Twenty minutes a day, no headphones. The smallest practice that changed the most.
posts.content:
## The pace

A walk is a thinking machine you wear with your shoes.

## The rule

No headphones. No phone. The point is the boredom; the boredom is the point.

posts.title: CSS I Keep Relearning
posts.excerpt: Margin collapse, stacking contexts, and the four properties I have to look up every single time.
posts.content:
## Margin collapse

Adjacent vertical margins collapse. It will surprise you again next month.

## Stacking contexts

`position: relative` does not create one. `z-index` on a non-positioned element does nothing.

## The four

`min-width: 0`, `flex-shrink`, `align-items: stretch`, and `overflow: clip`. I will look these up forever.

pages.title: About
pages.excerpt: A small journal about writing, design, and everyday tools.
pages.content:
This sample site uses the blog theme included with ZeroPress. Explore its posts, nested navigation, search, and sidebar widgets before publishing your own content.

## Publish your site

Follow **Deploy and connect Studio** in your repository's README. Your first publication replaces this page and the rest of the sample data with the content you manage in Studio.

## Make it yours

Manage menus in the `primary` and `footer` slots, and widgets in the `sidebar` area. The primary menu supports three levels; the footer supports one.

You can also edit the layout and styles in the repository's `theme/` directory. Files in `public/` remain in place when Studio publishes new content.
